candidates.explanation: After verifying the reset hash and updating the user's password (user.password = password; usersService.update), the method never invalidates the user's existing sessions. Sessions (used by refreshToken via sessionService.updateByHash) remain valid, so already signed-in devices can keep refreshing tokens after a reset. It needs to delete all sessions for the user (e.g. sessionService.deleteByUserId) after updating the password.
Password changes in update hash and persist the new password but do not revoke the user's sessions, so any caller (including reset password) leaves existing refresh sessions active.
Refresh only checks that the session exists and the user has a role; it does not check whether the password changed after the session was created, so sessions survive a password reset.

fix.description: In AuthService.resetPassword, after usersService.update(user.id, user), delete all of the user's sessions, e.g. await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id }), so every device must sign in again.
